title: This Is Now The ‘Worst Energy Crisis Ever’ | David Hay
speaker: David Hay (Haymaker Publications), interviewed by David Lin

macro_themes.view: Lost Gulf supply, plunging inventories and record crack spreads make this worse than 1979; futures underprice physical oil and there is no glut.
Rich-world bond markets are fragile from deficits and loose policy; yields could spike further (10y maybe 6%) before a stock selloff triggers a counter-trend bond rally.
Breadth is the worst in 30 years, CAPE ~41 and fund cash levels low; he is uncomfortable with stocks, expects a shakeout and eventually a severe bear market.
A blue sweep could see the president challenge results, an underappreciated market risk.
Data-center electricity demand and booming US LNG exports make cheap US natural gas a bargain; Europe faces a tough winter.
Raise some cash, ladder 2-10y Treasuries, buy Meta 20y bonds at ~7%, and buy beaten-down energy names.

calls.condition: Short-term pullback likely before resumption; $200 is a possibility, not a firm target
calls.reason: Spot ~$20 over the two-year forward usually brings a near-term correction within a rising trend; shortage, restocking and a post-midterm short squeeze could push oil toward $200 (gold/oil ratio).
calls.quote: you could see oil hit $200 a barrel. As I said earlier, that wouldn't be outlandish.

calls.condition: Buy on a pullback, especially in a market shakeout
calls.reason: Broke out above its 2013 high on a long-term chart after years of underinvestment; extended, so a pullback would be a buying opportunity.
calls.quote: on a pullback, you want to I think you want to be a buyer of energy.

calls.reason: Half its price of 12 years ago despite the energy boom, ~12x non-peak earnings; oil services follow producers in the cycle. He owns a lot and bought more.
calls.quote: I think Hallebertton is a terrific buy at this point and I own a lot personally and bought more recently.

calls.reason: Natural-gas producer in a gradual uptrend after a recent pullback (timely), P/E ~9.6, likely takeover target; plays data-center gas demand.
calls.quote: it's actually you know fairly timely and again like hell very inexpensively priced

calls.reason: Class-act midstream name yielding 6.2%, pulled back ~10% from its high; a way to play the US natural gas boom.
calls.quote: you could buy an EPD which is the class act in the midstream area

calls.reason: US gas at ~$3 vs 20+ in Europe/Asia, booming LNG exports and ~52 GW of data centers under construction drive demand.
calls.quote: I just can't believe that we're going to have gas this cheap in the United States and Canada.

calls.condition: If yields spike further, a stock crash would spark a powerful (counter-trend) bond rally
calls.reason: Yields broke multi-year resistance and are in a monster uptrend on fiscal deficits; may spike to ~6% near term, but higher yields likely trigger a stock selloff and a counter-trend bond rally ('rent, not own').
calls.quote: maybe the 10ear goes to six. But I think the higher those yields go, the more likely they are to trigger at least a stock …

calls.condition: Severe bear market is a longer-term expectation, not immediate
calls.reason: Worst breadth in 30 years, Hindenburg Omen clusters, low fund-manager cash and CAPE ~41; a shakeout looks likely and eventually a very severe bear market.
calls.quote: eventually I think that's going to lead to a very very severe bare market. I don't think that's right away

calls.condition: If the Fed panics and cuts short rates after a market break
calls.reason: Gold miners have been crushed; a Fed panic into rate cuts after a market break could spark a big move in inflation hedges.
